To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) adult survivors of childhood cancers are a growing and vulnerable patient population; (2) they are at risk for late effects of treatment; (3) they have unmet health needs; (4) they face significant barriers to health care; (5) they need a coordinated system to meet their needs, and (6) a national strategy is needed to address these challenges.

the health policy community has a poor understanding of the health care needs of adult survivors of childhood cancers, and that a number of barriers prevent survivors from receiving appropriate care, including the fragmentation of health care delivery, lack of coordination among health care providers, lack of knowledge of survivor care needs among primary care physicians, and lack of awareness among patients of their own health care needs.
